# Unicode character dispatch originals

MathJax 3.2.2's ordinary letter map accepts ASCII `a`–`z` and `A`–`Z`. Non-ASCII characters continue through the source range dispatch. Candidate `0158db95` restores that distinction instead of classifying every Unicode letter as an ordinary identifier; the existing operator-letter handling remains in place.

The focused corpus preserves 972 complete original inputs: 868 source-valid SVGs and 104 original runtime exceptions. A separate supplement preserves 40 existing source records: 38 raw U+207F residuals promoted to strict original-SVG assertions, plus two existing strict phantom controls. The combined 1,012 public inputs contain 908 strict SVG assertions, comprising 560 semantic repairs and 348 controls. Relative to actual merged PR181 (`6d88373d`), these are 840 first SVG inputs, 38 first strict assertions for existing raw inputs, and 30 prior strict references. No original error SVG, unsafe XML, or held SVG occurs in these fixtures.

The supplement retains each complete historical source record, source Git identity, JSON pointer, memberships and source-file metadata. Its expected SVG is exclusively the historical `original.svg` for raw residuals or `svg` for strict phantom controls. Historical Go baseline/candidate fields remain unchanged as provenance and never supply expectations. The original residual and strict fixture files and their existing consumers remain unchanged. The focused five containers and both native profiles also remain unchanged from the earlier focused draft.

The 104 full historical exceptions are retained separately and are not SVG parity cases. Of these, 98 null-range inputs use source-derived bounded API diagnostics (58 newly bounded and 40 controls). Six supplementary-CJK inputs fail in the original renderer under its literal `normnal` variant; their tests check successful Go fallback without a Go-produced expected SVG or hash. The candidate audit separately establishes complete baseline/candidate equality for those six. Runtime publication accounting is 98 first inputs and six prior bounded guards, a different partition from exception kind.

The native documents retain 152 pilot and 72 range observations on distinct existing focused inputs. Every original/observed output, event, request and schema is preserved. They add no public inputs and do not claim that Go reproduces JavaScript event traces. The public tests assert 908 complete original SVG strings, 98 bounded API contracts and six weaker successful-fallback contracts.

`generate_unicode_character_owner.cjs` pins the three frozen MathJax 3.2.2 assets and recorded Node executable. Authorized regeneration uses a fresh VM for each of 1,012 original conversions and 448 native plain/observed conversions: 1,460 in total. Both observer bodies are retained byte-for-byte. The shared encoder produces the same fixed-header, level-9 gzip bytes during export and regeneration for all six containers. The generator preserves full historical runtime objects and writes every complete fresh exception separately before comparing the source frames; historical stacks are never replaced to manufacture equality. Each complete public or native conversion is appended immediately to `fresh-observations.jsonl`. After the synchronous conversion and detached snapshot, the sequential loop yields to the event loop before creating the next VM, allowing startup promise jobs to drain and completed contexts to be collected. VM setup, observer installation and conversion are never separated by a yield.

Expanded protection independently qualified the 38 supplemental Unicode repairs with no source/consumer regressions or runtime changes. Four cancellation attribute-order samples are preserved in the broader audit and excluded from repair counts. That audit covers 145,489 distinct requests and 163,355 source memberships, with 2,035 unchanged source-runtime inputs. These figures describe the measured audit, not universal MathJax parity or additional fixture assertions.

Status: original-only regeneration reproduced all six containers byte for byte, with 1,460 fresh conversions and full fresh exception evidence retained. The generator drains the event loop between completed conversions; every render still uses a fresh VM. The formatted public Go tests, full frozen-oracle suite, race tests with a 20 minute timeout, vet and WebAssembly build passed at `e40e4a3ef4cbc12877207e1ef03381f74f475ec9`. Production and dependencies match source `0158db95a3c1d3bec582320314ad1679fa469a61`; subsequent publication metadata leaves tests, generators, fixtures and image bytes unchanged.
